canonicalExplanation.summary: Borders, shadows, gradients and background images make surfaces feel polished — but they're **decoration**. Layer them safely: set a **solid background-color first** as a fallback, add gradients or images on top, and keep text contrast measured against the worst case. Never put required information (instructions, prices, labels) inside a background image: it can't be read by screen readers, translated, selected or zoomed cleanly, and it ignores users' forced high-contrast colours.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A promo banner's instructions — "Use code WELCOME10 at checkout" — are baked into its background image. Screen readers skip it, translation tools can't see it, and on a slow network the image hasn't loaded, leaving an empty coloured box. A decorative gradient sits over a solid fallback colour, while all instructional text remains real HTML. In this lesson you'll implement a visual surface treatment that degrades safely and preserves readability.

```predict
{"question": "Text that's part of a CSS background-image — can a screen reader read it?", "options": ["Yes", "No — background images have no text alternative"], "answer": 1, "why": "Background images are decoration only. Important text must be real HTML text."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Lengths, percentages and viewport units**, **Paragraph and inline meaning**, **Color and contrast**, and **Content, padding, border and margin**.

sections.heading: The model: solid base, decorative layers, real text on top
sections.body:
```css .banner { background-color: #1e3a8a; /* fallback: always present */ background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, rgb(30 58 138 / 0.9), rgb(124 58 237 / 0.85)), url("/img/waves.svg"); /* decorative */ background-size: cover; color: #ffffff; /* measured vs darkest AND lightest spot */ border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.15); border: 1px solid transparent; /* visible in forced-colours mode */ } ``` ```html

Welcome offer

Use code WELCOME10 at checkout.

``` | Layer | Role | |---|---| | background-color. | shown if images fail or before they load. | | gradient/image. | decoration. | | real text. | readable, translatable, selectable. | | transparent border. | keeps an outline in high-contrast modes. | ```reveal {"prompt": "Why a transparent border?", "answer": "In Windows forced-colours (high contrast) mode, background colours, gradients and shadows are replaced or removed, but borders get the system colour — so the box's edge stays visible."} ```

sections.heading: Shadows and borders carry no meaning alone

includes: Layer backgrounds, gradients, borders and shadows over a solid fallback colour.
Keep instructional text in HTML and check readability when images fail or colours are forced.

outcomes: Implement a visual surface treatment that degrades safely and preserves readability.

examples.title: A gradient over a solid fallback
examples.situation: A decorative gradient sits over a solid fallback color while all instructional text remains real HTML.
walkthrough: **Solid fallback colour:** `background-color: #1e3a8a` renders immediately, even before or without images.
**Decorative gradient:** layered on top through background-image, purely for looks.
**Real HTML text:** "Use code WELCOME10 at checkout" is a paragraph, measured at 4.5:1+ against both gradient ends; images disabled, the browser will still render readable text.
examples.result: The banner looks rich when everything loads, and stays readable and usable when it doesn't.

examples.title: The image-only price tag
examples.situation: A sale badge is a PNG containing "50% OFF — today only" set as a background image on an empty span.
walkthrough: Screen readers, search engines and translation tools get nothing.
Zooming makes the text blurry, and the PNG ignores a user's forced high-contrast colours.
Fix: real text in the span (`50% off — today only`) styled with CSS colours and borders.
examples.result: The badge is readable by everyone and scales crisply.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: A background image is an appropriate place for required instructions, because it cannot be selected.
misconceptions.correction: Background images have no text alternative, can't be translated or zoomed cleanly, may not load, and don't adapt to forced-colours mode. Required information must be real HTML text; backgrounds are decoration.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The image-only price tag", who missed the sale information?

analogy.example: A background is like **wallpaper**: nice, but you don't write the fire-exit instructions on it in faint pattern. The instructions go on a proper sign (HTML text) that everyone can read even if the wallpaper is torn down.
usefulFor: solid colour as the wall underneath
limitations: Wallpaper can't fail to load; images can.
Forced-colours mode is like painting over the wallpaper.

steps.explanation: The solid fallback colour appears first.
A decorative gradient sits over the solid fallback colour.
All instructional text remains real HTML and is measured against the gradient.

trace.textAlternative: Layering a banner safely. Step 1, Fallback: images is not loaded; background is #1e3a8a; text is readable. The solid fallback colour appears first. Step 2, Decoration: gradient is over fallback. A decorative gradient sits over the solid fallback colour. Step 3, Text: instructions is real HTML; contrast is ≥ 4.5:1 on both ends. All instructional text remains real HTML and is measured against the gradient.

faded.prompt: For "A gradient over a solid fallback", explain why a decorative gradient sits over a solid fallback color while all instructional text remains real HTML.
expectedEvidence: Names the example "A gradient over a solid fallback": a decorative gradient sits over a solid fallback color.
The fallback shows if images fail or are slow.
All instructional text remains real HTML.
Text contrast is measured against both gradient ends, so the banner looks rich when everything loads and stays readable when it doesn't.

nearTransfer.prompt: A card uses a photo background with white text. List three things you'd add so the text stays readable.
expectedEvidence: A dark background-color fallback and a translucent overlay gradient.
Measure text against the lightest area; transparent border for forced colours.

farTransfer.prompt: Style a hero section with a gradient, image and shadow. Test with images blocked, in forced-colours mode (DevTools emulation) and at 200% zoom; fix anything unreadable.
scaffold: Block images in the Network panel.
expectedEvidence: Hero readable in all three tests.
Notes on what changed to make it robust.

remediation.explanation: Turn off images and emulate forced colours. Anything that disappears was decoration — check that no information went with it.
remediation.retryPrompt: Test "The image-only price tag" this way.

recap.summary: To implement a visual surface treatment that degrades safely, set a solid fallback background-color, layer gradients and images as decoration, keep all instructional text in real HTML with measured contrast, and add borders that survive forced-colours mode.
retrievalPrompts: Why set background-color under a gradient?
Why must instructions not be in background images?
